commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". 1	"""Story S-114: a gentle wind-down nudge before the user's usual bedtime."""
2	
3	from dataclasses import dataclass
4	from datetime import UTC, date, datetime, time, timedelta
5	from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
6	
7	from nightjar.claims import load_register
8	from nightjar.models import Night, User, zone
9	from nightjar.sleep_window import usual_bedtime
10	
11	
12	@dataclass(frozen=True)
13	class Nudge:
14	    at: datetime  # aware, in the user's current time zone
15	    silent: bool  # True during quiet hours: deliver without sound, don't skip
16	    text: str
17	
18	
19	def next_nudge(user: User, nights: list[Night], now: datetime) -> Nudge | None:
20	    """The next wind-down nudge after `now`, or None on a cold start (< 7 nights)."""
21	    if now.tzinfo is None:
22	        raise ValueError("now must be timezone-aware")
23	    bedtime = usual_bedtime(nights)
24	    if bedtime is None:
25	        return None
26	
27	    user_zone = zone(user.timezone)  # the user's *current* zone (AC2)
28	    nudge_time = clock_minus(bedtime, timedelta(minutes=user.wind_down_lead_minutes))
29	    today = now.astimezone(user_zone).date()
30	    at = at_local_time(today, nudge_time, user_zone)
31	    if at.astimezone(UTC) <= now.astimezone(UTC):  # compare instants, not wall clocks
32	        at = at_local_time(today + timedelta(days=1), nudge_time, user_zone)
33	
34	    return Nudge(
35	        at=at,
36	        silent=in_quiet_hours(user, at.time()),  # delivered wall time, not the nominal one
37	        text=nudge_text(bedtime, at.date()),
38	    )
39	
40	
41	def at_local_time(day: date, clock_time: time, user_zone: ZoneInfo) -> datetime:
42	    """`clock_time` on `day` in `user_zone`.
43	
44	    The UTC round trip normalises wall times that DST skips (02:30 on
45	    spring-forward day becomes 03:30) so the result is a real instant.
46	    """
47	    wall_clock = datetime.combine(day, clock_time, tzinfo=user_zone)
48	    return wall_clock.astimezone(UTC).astimezone(user_zone)
49	
50	
51	def clock_minus(clock_time: time, delta: timedelta) -> time:
52	    """Time-of-day arithmetic that wraps around midnight (00:10 - 45 min = 23:25)."""
53	    start = datetime.combine(date(2000, 1, 2), clock_time, tzinfo=UTC)
54	    return (start - delta).time()
55	
56	
57	def in_quiet_hours(user: User, clock_time: time) -> bool:
58	    start, end = user.quiet_start, user.quiet_end
59	    if start is None or end is None:
60	        return False
61	    if start <= end:
62	        return start <= clock_time < end
63	    return clock_time >= start or clock_time < end  # window wraps midnight
64	
65	
66	def nudge_text(bedtime: time, day: date) -> str:
67	    """Pick approved copy from the claims register (AC4); it varies by day."""
68	    templates = load_register()["nudge_copy"]
69	    template = templates[day.toordinal() % len(templates)]
70	    return template.format(bedtime=bedtime.strftime("%H:%M"))
71

# NightJar claims register
# Owner: Regulatory & Brand (fictional team). Changes need their review.
# NightJar is a wellness product, not a medical device. User-facing copy may
# use approved wellness phrases and must never match a banned pattern.
version: 3

approved_phrases:
  - wind down
  - relax
  - build a consistent bedtime routine
  - keep a regular sleep schedule
  - get ready for bed
  - a calm evening
  - rest

# Nudge copy (story S-114, AC4). {bedtime} is the user's usual bedtime, e.g. 23:00.
nudge_copy:
  - "Time to wind down. Your usual bedtime is {bedtime}."
  - "A gentle reminder to relax and get ready for bed. Your usual bedtime is {bedtime}."
  - "Start a calm evening and wind down. Your usual bedtime is {bedtime}."

# Banned disease-claim patterns (Python regular expressions, case-insensitive).
banned:
  - id: disease-insomnia
    pattern: '\binsomnia\b'
    reason: Names a sleep disorder.
  - id: disease-sleep-apnea
    pattern: '\bsleep\s+apnoea\b|\bsleep\s+apnea\b|\bapnea\b'
    reason: Names a sleep disorder.
  - id: claim-treat
    pattern: '\btreat(s|ed|ing|ment|ments)?\b'
    reason: Implies medical treatment.
  - id: claim-cure
    pattern: '\bcur(e|es|ed|ing)\b'
    reason: Implies a cure.
  - id: claim-diagnose
    pattern: '\bdiagnos\w*'
    reason: Implies a diagnosis.
  - id: disease-anxiety-disorder
    pattern: '\banxiety\s+disorders?\b'
    reason: Names a mental health condition.
  - id: claim-prescribe
    pattern: '\bprescri(be|bes|bed|ption|ptions)\b'
    reason: Implies prescribing.
  - id: claim-clinically-proven
    pattern: '\bclinically\s+proven\b'
    reason: Unsupported efficacy claim.
claims/register.yaml
